name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean anchors the seat firmly in Republican territory
Jackson's roughly 40-to-1 cash advantage ($5.4M vs $14K on hand)
Incumbent renominated; no polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive
Prediction markets price Jackson near 94% to hold the seat
model.rationale: The district's 23-point Republican lean, Jackson's overwhelming financial advantage, and the absence of any polling, expert ratings, or visible challenger momentum all point to a safe Republican hold, and markets agree at roughly 94% for Jackson.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Jackson or a sudden influx of Democratic outside spending could narrow the race, though nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 13th District sits deep in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Ronny Jackson, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a commanding financial position: about $5.4 million on hand after raising more than $4 million, plus modest outside support. Democrat Mark Nair has raised roughly $102,000 and had about $14,000 in the bank at the last reporting deadline, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and betting markets give Jackson about a 94% chance of holding the seat. With the challenger badly underfunded and no evidence of a local dynamic favoring Democrats, the seat remains safely in Republican hands this cycle.
